h.replay_of_her_seeded_code.note: Her own gendata() and lm() on her own seeded datasets (r-reproduction, literal check identical). With 50 replications a condition mean has Monte Carlo error up to about .03 at n = 500.

h.interaction_dropped_from_the_fitted_mo.prediction: if her y model omitted tm, b-hat would absorb the interaction (b + h times the treated share), so her PNIE bias would carry a positive a*h term that grows with the treated share
h.interaction_dropped_from_the_fitted_mo.finding: the a*h and h coefficients of her PNIE bias are zero to three decimals at every cutoff

h.which_no_interaction_mechanism.finding: only the intercept differs (by h); t, r, m and tm coefficients are identical, so a y generated before tm was filled in and a y generated with h = 0 give the same a, b, c' and h estimates. The published results cannot tell these two apart; her y intercepts were not reported.

population.condition_level_value_wrong.prediction: a wrong population value per condition (for example ab(1 + k)) would let coverage fall toward 0 as n grows, because the interval shrinks around the estimate while the value stays away
population.condition_level_value_wrong.finding: coverage falls with n only to a plateau at about the control share (.25, .49, .74 from n = 2,500), not toward 0; ruled out

population.per_case_value_by_treatment.prediction: if the population value were computed per case and was right for control cases but not for treated ones, coverage averaged over cases would fall with n (wide intervals still cover some treated cases) to a plateau near the control share, imbalance 'above' would approach the treated share and 'below' a small fraction of the control share, and bias would be -lambda x treated share x the path product with one lambda for all cutoffs
population.per_case_value_by_treatment.finding: coverage plateaus at the control share and imbalance above at the treated share at every cutoff, with below at .008-.017; the bias multipliers fit with lambda = 1.959, 1.918, 1.764 (cutoffs 1-3), close for cutoffs 1-2 but not constant, so the same rule does not reproduce cutoff 3 exactly

pnde.definition.her_definition: PNDE = c' + h (printed p. 104); the true value under her data-generating model is c' + h * i0M with i0M = 0
pnde.definition.finding: with h-hat near 0, a population value of c' + h predicts a PNDE bias coefficient of -1 on h; the fits give about -0.93 (PNDE) and -1.0 (TNDE)

statements.residuals.text: PNIE Type I outside the robustness criteria at n = 500 and 1000, within for larger n, when b = 0 and a = .14, at all cutoffs
TNIE3 Type I outside the robustness criteria at n = 1000 when a = 0, b = .14, h = 0 or .05
TNIE Type I within the robustness criteria in all other cases with a = 0 (b or h nonzero, apart from the TNIE3 exceptions)
TNIE2 and TNIE3 power show overall patterns similar to TNIE1 (read as: no differences across the three cutoffs; h = .15, every a and b)
TNDE1 power around .80 at n = 500 and above .80 at larger n when c' = .39, at all a and h
TNDE power shows no variation by cutoff (h = .15)
TNDE2 and TNDE3 power show overall patterns similar to TNDE1 (read as: no differences across the three cutoffs; every c', a and h with a nonzero TNDE)

tnde.power_gap.cells: TNDE, cutoff 1, n = 500, c' = .39, a = .59, h = 0 (averaged over b)
tnde.power_gap.note: her_code_* use the 50-replication replay (#92); the full_replay block uses all 1,000 (#118)

n5000.both_paths_zero.finding: with both paths zero the product test is conservative at every n, in her own figure as in ours; no sample size brings these cells into Bradley's range

headstart.sb_divisor.note: see secondary/table_arithmetic.py: the differences match; the standardized biases match only with the RCT estimate's SE as divisor
